Live gate over HTTP /@fs/ + query-suffix payloads: reads flag@v0, blocked@v1, ?raw?import residual reads flag@v1 (blocked@v2 per repro). passed=true.

evidence.fix_reference: npm:vite@5.4.15 (node:20-slim, Dockerfile ARG VITE_VERSION); npm:vite@5.4.16 (node:20-slim, Dockerfile ARG VITE_VERSION)
evidence.incomplete_fix_quote: The contents of arbitrary files can be returned to the browser. base64 encoded content of non-allowed files is exposed using `?inline&import` (originally reported as `?import&?inline=1.wasm?init`); content of non-allowed files is exposed using `?raw?import`. This is a residual of the CVE-2025-30208 fix, whose rawRE/urlRE guard only matched `raw`/`url` at the query end or before `&`, so `?raw?import` and `?inline` slipped past the serving-access check.

provenance.notes: Real Docker verification: node:20-slim + npm i vite@5.4.14/5.4.15/5.4.16, minimal Vite dev server (`vite --host`), canary planted at /canary.txt (outside project root) via compose entrypoint. Gate run 2026-07-11 via `python3 oracle.py --run-gate`; see repro.log. Mechanism from patch.diff (packages/vite/src/node/server/middlewares/transform.ts): CVE-2025-30208 fix (5.4.15) strips trailing `[?&]+$` then runs rawRE/urlRE + ensureServingAccess, blocking `?import&raw??` (403 on 5.4.15, was 200 on 5.4.14); but those guard regexes only matched `raw` at query-end/before `&`, so the residual `?raw?import` skips the guard and still reads the canary (200 on 5.4.15). CVE-2025-31125 fix (5.4.16) replaces them with /[?&]raw\b/ + inlineRE, closing the residual (403 on 5.4.16). Images deleted after gate (down --rmi all + prune).
